snapshot.stmt: Fix \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\). The aggregate formed from the Ortiz-Villavicencio--Sant'Anna componentwise-GMM ATT estimators using the prespecified weights is joint-optimal if and only if \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), equivalently if and only if each block of \(\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) is constant across the comparison cohorts in that block. For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\), with \(P=Q_O\), \[V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}(N^{\prime}\Omega N)^{-1}(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})=(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}}).\] Thus \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}\) has strictly smaller asymptotic variance than \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}\) exactly when the net cross-block covariance contribution is nonconstant across comparison cohorts within at least one group-event block. For \(g=2\), all covariance entries use the defined baseline period \(1\). If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), then \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}=b^{\mathrm{sep}}\), and \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\), reproducing within-cell GMM optimality.

defs.def:ddd-law-class: \(\mathcal M=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathsf W): Q\text{ satisfies consistency, no anticipation, no ineligible spillover, every retained pairwise conditional DDD restriction, cell overlap with }0<\varepsilon<1/4,\text{ and, for }P=Q_O,\text{ the fourth-moment, true-regression fourth-moment, and score-spectrum bounds}\}\). The class contains only primitive restrictions on \(Q\) and its observed-data pushforward \(P\); independent sampling, cross-fitting, and learner rates are theorem-level conditions.
defs.def:pairwise-score: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), set \[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)=\Theta_k(P)+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\pi_{g,1}}\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}+\frac{p_{g,1}(X_i)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{p_{a,s}(X_i)}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\}.\] Thus \(R_{k,c}-\Theta_k(P)\) is the observed-data first-order influence of the Hájek-ratio pairwise estimator, including estimation of \(\pi_{g,1}\).
defs.def:observable-functional: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), define \[\Theta_k(P)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal J_k|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal J_k}\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}},\qquad \Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)=\omega^{\prime}\Theta(P).\] Both quantities are functionals only of the observed-data law \(P=Q_O\).
defs.def:separate-loading: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \[(b^{\mathrm{sep}})_k=\omega_k\frac{\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1},\] and \(b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) stacks these blocks. This is exactly the loading produced by optimizing each group-event cell separately and then applying \(\omega\).

assumptions.ass:no-anticipation: \(Q\{Y_{it}(g,1)=Y_{it}(\infty,1)\text{ for every }g\in\mathcal G\text{ and }t\in\mathcal T\text{ with }t<g\}=1\).
assumptions.ass:pairwise-conditional-ddd: For every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\) with \(2\le g\le t\le T\), every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(Q_X\)-almost every \(x\), \(E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,1)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,1)\mid G_i=g,S_i=1,X_i=x]-E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,0)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,0)\mid G_i=g,S_i=0,X_i=x]=E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,1)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,1)\mid G_i=c,S_i=1,X_i=x]-E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,0)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,0)\mid G_i=c,S_i=0,X_i=x]\).
assumptions.ass:cell-overlap: For every cohort-eligibility cell \((a,s)\) entering a retained comparison, \(Q(G_i=a,S_i=s\mid X_i=x)\ge\varepsilon\) for \(Q_X\)-almost every \(x\).

snapshot.stmt:
Label-preserving equivalence classes of \(\mathfrak H(P)\) split exactly into the equality class
\[
 \mathscr E_0=\{[\mathfrak H(P)]:N'\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)=0\}
\]
and its complement \(\mathscr E_+\), on which the joint variance gain is strictly positive whenever the invariant is induced by a compatible law in \(\mathcal M\).  This is a complete classification because all entries of the displayed diagnostic are components or computable functions of the labelled invariant.

The complement is nonempty even in the smallest architecture in the question.  In particular, take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/8\).  For any prespecified \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)'\) with \(\omega_1+\omega_2=1\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\), there is a bounded compatible full-data law \(Q\in\mathcal M\) for which, in the coordinate order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
 \Omega=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 3/8&3/16&0\\
 3/16&3/8&3/32\\
 0&3/32&3/8
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 b^{\mathrm{sep}}=(\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)',
\]
and
\[
 V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=\frac{3\omega_2^2}{128}>0.
\]

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), suppose the off-fold learners satisfy foldwise independence, the fitted-regression \(L_4(P_X)\) envelope, \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\), \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\), \(a_n\to0\), \(b_n\to0\), and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). Four disjoint cells enter each retained pairwise score, so overlap and \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\) give \(p_{a,s}(x)\in[\varepsilon,1-3\varepsilon]\subset[\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]\) for every retained cell. Hence \(C_\varepsilon(p_{a,s})=p_{a,s}\), the clipping map is one-Lipschitz, and \[\|\widetilde p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\le\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n).\] The outcome and true-regression fourth-moment envelopes give \(\|\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O(1)\), and the fitted regressions are uniformly \(L_4\)-bounded by hypothesis. For each residual term, clipping, the Lipschitz bound for \((u,v)\mapsto u/v\) on \([\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]^2\), and H"older's inequality yield \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\left(\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}-\frac{p_{g,1}}{p_{a,s}}\right)(\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\left(\|\widetilde p_{g,1}-p_{g,1}\|_{P_X,4}+\|\widetilde p_{a,s}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\right)\|\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O_P(a_n),\] and \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}(\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\|\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(b_n).\] The fitted target-contrast term is bounded by the sum of its four regression errors. Conditional score bias is bounded by \(C_\varepsilon\max_{p,m}\|\widehat p-p\|_{P_X,2}\|\widehat m-m\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(a_nb_n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\); foldwise independence makes every centered validation-fold plug-in fluctuation \(o_P(1)\) after \(n^{-1/2}\) summation. The empirical target share is root-\(n\) consistent, lies in the interior clipping region with probability tending to one, and its ratio expansion supplies exactly the target-share term in \(\Psi\). Therefore, uniformly over the fixed score coordinates, \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\mu-B\Theta(P)\}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1),\qquad \max_{1\le j\le M}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\}^2=o_P(1).\]

Define \[\widehat A_{i,k,c}=\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\widehat d_{k,c,i}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\},\qquad \widehat\mu_{k,c}=\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat A_{i,k,c}}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}},\] and display the fitted influence coordinate \[\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}=\frac{1}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\{\widehat d_{k,c,i}-\widehat\mu_{k,c}\}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\}\right].\] Stack \(\widehat\mu_{k,c}\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}\). snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), impose the theorem-level foldwise independence, fitted-regression \(L_4\) envelope, propensity and regression \(L_4\) rates, and product-rate condition. The score expansion lemma gives \(D_{i,j}=\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\) with \(\max_j n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2=o_P(1)\). For every \(1\le j,q\le M\), expand the exact displayed covariance estimator entrywise as \[\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}=\left\{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right\}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,j}\widehat\Psi_{i,q}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)D_{i,q}.\] The oracle empirical-covariance fluctuation is \(o_P(1)\) by i.i.d. sampling and the fourth-moment envelopes. Cauchy--Schwarz gives \[\begin{aligned}|\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}|&\le\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right|\\&\quad+\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}+\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\Psi_j(O_i)^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}=o_P(1),\end{aligned}\] where \(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_{i,q}^2=O_P(1)\) follows from \(\widehat\Psi_{i,q}=\Psi_q(O_i)+D_{i,q}\). Since \(M\) is fixed, \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M\max_{j,q}|A_{jq}|\) passes entrywise convergence to operator norm. Because \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^M\) and positive-semidefinite projection is nonexpansive in Frobenius norm, \[\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),\qquad \|\widehat\Omega_\lambda-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\lambda_n=o_P(1).\]

defs.def:ddd-law-class: \(\mathcal M=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathsf W): Q\text{ satisfies consistency, no anticipation, no ineligible spillover, every retained pairwise conditional DDD restriction, cell overlap with }0<\varepsilon<1/4,\text{ and, for }P=Q_O,\text{ the fourth-moment, true-regression fourth-moment, and score-spectrum bounds}\}\). The class contains only primitive restrictions on \(Q\) and its observed-data pushforward \(P\); independent sampling, cross-fitting, and learner rates are theorem-level conditions.
defs.def:joint-estimator: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and observation \(i\), first set \(\widetilde p_{a,s,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde p_{g,1,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{g,1,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde\pi_{g,1}=C_\varepsilon(n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_j=g,S_j=1\})\), and \(\widehat d_{k,c,i}=\widehat m_{g,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{g,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{c,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)+\widehat m_{c,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\). Define \[\widehat A_{i,k,c}=\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\widehat d_{k,c,i}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\},\qquad \widehat\mu_{k,c}=\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat A_{i,k,c}}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}},\] and display the fitted influence coordinate \[\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}=\frac{1}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\{\widehat d_{k,c,i}-\widehat\mu_{k,c}\}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\}\right].\] Stack \(\widehat\mu_{k,c}\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}\). Set \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_i\widehat\Psi_i^{\prime}\), \(\widehat\Omega=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^M}(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}})\), and \(\widehat\Omega_\lambda=\widehat\Omega+n^{-1/4}I_M\). For each \(k\), set \(\widehat b_k^{\mathrm{sep}}=\omega_k\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\), and set \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega\). Finally, \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\). Every denominator and inverse in this construction is defined for every realized sample.
defs.def:separate-loading: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \[(b^{\mathrm{sep}})_k=\omega_k\frac{\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1},\] and \(b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) stacks these blocks. This is exactly the loading produced by optimizing each group-event cell separately and then applying \(\omega\).
defs.def:pairwise-score: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), set \[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)=\Theta_k(P)+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\pi_{g,1}}\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}+\frac{p_{g,1}(X_i)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{p_{a,s}(X_i)}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\}.\] Thus \(R_{k,c}-\Theta_k(P)\) is the observed-data first-order influence of the Hájek-ratio pairwise estimator, including estimation of \(\pi_{g,1}\).
defs.def:observable-functional: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), define \[\Theta_k(P)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal J_k|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal J_k}\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}},\qquad \Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)=\omega^{\prime}\Theta(P).\] Both quantities are functionals only of the observed-data law \(P=Q_O\).

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\), let \(P=Q_O\). Suppose the off-fold learners satisfy foldwise independence, \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(1)\), \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\), \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\), \(a_n\to0\), \(b_n\to0\), and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). Use the deterministic ridge \(\lambda_n=n^{-1/4}>0\). The score expansion and covariance lemmas then derive, rather than assume, \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}-\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\}=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n(b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1)\rightsquigarrow N(0,V_{\mathrm{joint}}),\qquad \|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1).\] The normal limit follows from the i.i.d. unit-level influence sum and the primitive fourth-moment envelope. Moreover, \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}\) is the unique minimizer of \(b^{\prime}\Omega b\) over constant \(b\in\mathbb R^M\) satisfying \(B^{\prime}b=\omega\), \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\to_Pb^{\mathrm{joint}}\), \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{joint}}>0\), and \[\lim_{n\to\infty}P\{\tau_\omega(Q)\in\mathcal C_{n,1-\alpha}\}=1-\alpha.\] If a target coordinate has \(g=2\), its score and fitted score use \(\Delta Y_{i,k}=Y_{it}-Y_{i1}\). If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), the joint loading, estimator, and variance reduce to the published within-\(k\) comparison-cohort GMM objects. The zero-variance convention in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:wald-interval}\) totalizes the finite-sample interval and is asymptotically inactive.

snapshot.stmt:
Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/8\). Fix \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)^{\prime}\) with \(\omega_1+\omega_2=1\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\). For every
\[
0<|\rho|<\frac{\sqrt7}{3}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
0<|\delta|<\frac18,
\]
there is a bounded compatible law \(Q_{\rho,\delta}\in\mathcal M\), with nonzero constant post-adoption effects equal to \(\delta\), for which, in the coordinate order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
\Omega(\rho)=
\begin{pmatrix}
3/8&3/16&0\\
3/16&3/8&3\rho/16\\
0&3\rho/16&3/8
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
b^{\mathrm{sep}}=
\begin{pmatrix}\omega_1/2\\ \omega_1/2\\ \omega_2\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
b^{\mathrm{joint}}=
\begin{pmatrix}
\omega_1/2+\rho\omega_2/2\\
\omega_1/2-\rho\omega_2/2\\
\omega_2
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}
=\frac{3\rho^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0.
\]
Thus the smallest architecture contains a nondegenerate open two-parameter family of strict-gap laws, rather than only a zero-effect isolated witness.

Under the sampling, sample-splitting, learner-envelope, nuisance-rate, product-rate, and ridge hypotheses of Theorem \(\ref{thm:joint-system-limit}\), the feasible diagnostic
\[
\widehat\Delta=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
\widehat\Omega
(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})
\]
is nonnegative for every realized sample and satisfies
\[
\widehat\Delta\to_P V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}.
\]

\widehat\Omega

Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\), and \(M\). The aggregate formed from the Ortiz-Villavicencio--Sant'Anna componentwise-GMM ATT functionals using the prespecified weights is joint-optimal in the constant retained-score span if and only if \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), equivalently if and only if each block of \(\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) is constant across the comparison cohorts in that block. \[

=(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}(N^{\prime}\Omega N)^{-1}(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})
=(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})
\]
holds without learner conditions. Suppose in addition that the i.i.d. sampling, fixed-fold sample splitting, fitted-regression \(L_4(P_X)\) envelope, propensity and regression \(L_4(P_X)\) rates, product-rate condition, and deterministic ridge condition of Theorem \(\ref{thm:joint-system-limit}\) all hold. For \(g=2\), all covariance entries use the defined baseline period \(1\). If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), then \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}=b^{\mathrm{sep}}\), and \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\), reproducing within-cell GMM optimality.

The complement is nonempty even in the smallest architecture in the question. \[

 \end{pmatrix},

 b^{\mathrm{sep}}=(\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)',

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), suppose the off-fold learners satisfy foldwise independence, the fitted-regression \(L_4(P_X)\) envelope, \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\), \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\), \(a_n\to0\), \(b_n\to0\), and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). Four disjoint cells enter each retained pairwise score, so overlap and \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\) give \(p_{a,s}(x)\in[\varepsilon,1-3\varepsilon]\subset[\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]\) for every retained cell. Hence \(C_\varepsilon(p_{a,s})=p_{a,s}\), the clipping map is one-Lipschitz, and \[\|\widetilde p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\le\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n).\] The outcome and true-regression fourth-moment envelopes give \(\|\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O(1)\), and the fitted regressions are uniformly \(L_4\)-bounded by hypothesis. For each residual term, clipping, the Lipschitz bound for \((u,v)\mapsto u/v\) on \([\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]^2\), and H"older's inequality yield \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\left(\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}-\frac{p_{g,1}}{p_{a,s}}\right)(\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\left(\|\widetilde p_{g,1}-p_{g,1}\|_{P_X,4}+\|\widetilde p_{a,s}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\right)\|\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O_P(a_n),\] and \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}(\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\|\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(b_n).\] The fitted target-contrast term is bounded by the sum of its four regression errors. Conditional score bias is bounded by \(C_\varepsilon\max_{p,m}\|\widehat p-p\|_{P_X,2}\|\widehat m-m\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(a_nb_n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\); foldwise independence makes every centered validation-fold plug-in fluctuation \(o_P(1)\) after \(n^{-1/2}\) summation. The empirical target share is root-\(n\) consistent, lies in the interior clipping region with probability tending to one, and its ratio expansion supplies exactly the target-share term in \(\Psi\). Therefore, uniformly over the fixed score coordinates, \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\mu-B\Theta(P)\}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1),\qquad \max_{1\le j\le M}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\}^2=o_P(1).\]

defs.def:ddd-law-class: \(\mathcal M=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathsf W): Q\text{ satisfies consistency, no anticipation, no ineligible spillover, every retained pairwise conditional DDD restriction, cell overlap with }0<\varepsilon<1/4,\text{ and, for }P=Q_O,\text{ the fourth-moment, true-regression fourth-moment, and score-spectrum bounds}\}\). The class contains only primitive restrictions on \(Q\) and its observed-data pushforward \(P\); independent sampling, cross-fitting, and learner rates are theorem-level conditions.
defs.def:joint-estimator:
For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and observation \(i\), first set \(\widetilde p_{a,s,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde p_{g,1,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{g,1,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde\pi_{g,1}=C_\varepsilon(n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_j=g,S_j=1\})\), and \(\widehat d_{k,c,i}=\widehat m_{g,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{g,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{c,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)+\widehat m_{c,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\). For each \(k\), set \(\widehat b_k^{\mathrm{sep}}=\omega_k\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\), and set \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega\). \[
\widehat\Delta=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
\widehat\Omega
(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}).
\]
Every denominator and inverse in this construction is defined for every realized sample, and \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) because \(\widehat\Omega\) is positive semidefinite.
defs.def:separate-loading: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \[(b^{\mathrm{sep}})_k=\omega_k\frac{\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1},\] and \(b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) stacks these blocks. snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), impose the theorem-level foldwise independence, fitted-regression \(L_4\) envelope, propensity and regression \(L_4\) rates, and product-rate condition. The score expansion lemma gives \(D_{i,j}=\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\) with \(\max_j n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2=o_P(1)\). Cauchy--Schwarz gives \[\begin{aligned}|\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}|&\le\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right|\\&\quad+\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}+\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\Psi_j(O_i)^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}=o_P(1),\end{aligned}\] where \(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_{i,q}^2=O_P(1)\) follows from \(\widehat\Psi_{i,q}=\Psi_q(O_i)+D_{i,q}\). Since \(M\) is fixed, \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M\max_{j,q}|A_{jq}|\) passes entrywise convergence to operator norm. Because \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^M\) and positive-semidefinite projection is nonexpansive in Frobenius norm, \[\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),\qquad \|\widehat\Omega_\lambda-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\lambda_n=o_P(1).\]

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\), let \(P=Q_O\). snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\), and \(M\). The aggregate formed from the Ortiz-Villavicencio--Sant'Anna componentwise-GMM ATT functionals using the prespecified weights is joint-optimal in the constant retained-score span if and only if \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), equivalently if and only if each block of \(\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) is constant across the comparison cohorts in that block. For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\), with \(P=Q_O\), the population identity
\[
V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}
=(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}(N^{\prime}\Omega N)^{-1}(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})
=(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})
\]
holds without learner conditions. Suppose in addition that the i.i.d. sampling, fixed-fold sample splitting, fitted-regression \(L_4(P_X)\) envelope, propensity and regression \(L_4(P_X)\) rates, product-rate condition, and deterministic ridge condition of Theorem \(\ref{thm:joint-system-limit}\) all hold. Then \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}\) and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}\) have asymptotic variances \(V_{\mathrm{joint}}\) and \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}\), respectively, so the joint estimator has strictly smaller asymptotic variance exactly when the net cross-block covariance contribution is nonconstant across comparison cohorts within at least one group-event block. Moreover, \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) for every realized sample and \(\widehat\Delta\to_P V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}\). Thus \(\widehat\Delta\) is a consistent descriptive diagnostic of the constant retained-score-span efficiency loss; no convergence rate, test, confidence interval, or full semiparametric-efficiency claim is made. For \(g=2\), all covariance entries use the defined baseline period \(1\). If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), then \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}=b^{\mathrm{sep}}\), and \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\), reproducing within-cell GMM optimality.

\[

\widehat\Omega
(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}).
\]

Label-preserving equivalence classes of \(\mathfrak H(P)\) split exactly into the equality class
\[
 \mathscr E_0=\{[\mathfrak H(P)]:N'\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)=0\}
\]
and its complement \(\mathscr E_+\), on which the joint variance gain is strictly positive whenever the invariant is induced by a compatible law in \(\mathcal M\).  This is a complete classification because all entries of the displayed diagnostic are components or computable functions of the labelled invariant.

The complement is nonempty even in the smallest architecture in the question.  In particular, take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/8\).  For any prespecified \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)'\) with \(\omega_1+\omega_2=1\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\), there is a bounded compatible full-data law \(Q\in\mathcal M\) for which, in the coordinate order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
 \Omega=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 3/8&3/16&0\\
 3/16&3/8&3/32\\
 0&3/32&3/8
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 b^{\mathrm{sep}}=(\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)',
\]
and
\[

\]

0&3\rho/16&3/8
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad

\begin{pmatrix}\omega_1/2\\ \omega_1/2\\ \omega_2\end{pmatrix},

\[

\begin{pmatrix}
\omega_1/2+\rho\omega_2/2\\
\omega_1/2-\rho\omega_2/2\\
\omega_2
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}
=\frac{3\rho^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0.
\]

Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3\}\), \(\omega_{(2,2)}=1\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/2\). Set \(Y_{it}(a,s)=U_{it}/8\) for every \(a\in\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), and \(t\in\{1,2,3\}\), and set \(Y_{it}=Y_{it}(G_i,S_i)\). The induced full-data law \(Q_0\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\): all four retained disjoint cells have probability \(1/4>\varepsilon\), the causal restrictions hold with zero effects and common trends, \(m_{a,s,(2,2)}=0\), and the sole centered score equals \(4\sigma_{a,s}^{2,3}\{U_{i2}-U_{i1}\}/8\) on cell \((a,s)\). Consequently, \(\Omega=1/2\), so \(\kappa I_1\preceq\Omega\preceq\kappa^{-1}I_1\), while the outcome and true-regression fourth-moment bounds hold.

defs.def:pairwise-score: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), set \[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)=\Theta_k(P)+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\pi_{g,1}}\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}+\frac{p_{g,1}(X_i)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{p_{a,s}(X_i)}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\}.\] Thus \(R_{k,c}-\Theta_k(P)\) is the observed-data first-order influence of the Hájek-ratio pairwise estimator, including estimation of \(\pi_{g,1}\).
defs.def:observable-functional: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), define \[\Theta_k(P)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal J_k|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal J_k}\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}},\qquad \Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)=\omega^{\prime}\Theta(P).\] Both quantities are functionals only of the observed-data law \(P=Q_O\).

snapshot.stmt: For every full-data law \(Q\in\mathcal M\), let \(P=Q_O=Q\circ o^{-1}\). defs.def:shared-covariance: For score coordinates \(j=(k,c)\) and \(q=(\ell,d)\), let \(g_k\) and \(g_\ell\) denote the first components of \(k\) and \(\ell\), and define \[\Omega^{\mathrm{DDD}}_{j q}=E_P\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{g_k=g_\ell\}p_{g_k,1}(X_i)\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}\{d_{\ell,d}(X_i)-\Theta_\ell(P)\}}{\pi_{g_k,1}\pi_{g_\ell,1}}+\sum_{a,s}p_{a,s}(X_i)L_{k,c}^{a,s}(X_i)L_{\ell,d}^{a,s}(X_i)v_{a,s;k\ell}(X_i)\right].\] The sum ranges over cohort-eligibility cells entering both score coordinates.

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), suppose the off-fold learners satisfy foldwise independence, the fitted-regression \(L_4(P_X)\) envelope, \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\), \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\), \(a_n\to0\), \(b_n\to0\), and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). Four disjoint cells enter each retained pairwise score, so overlap and \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\) give \(p_{a,s}(x)\in[\varepsilon,1-3\varepsilon]\subset[\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]\) for every retained cell. Hence \(C_\varepsilon(p_{a,s})=p_{a,s}\), the clipping map is one-Lipschitz, and \[\|\widetilde p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\le\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n).\] The outcome and true-regression fourth-moment envelopes give \(\|\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O(1)\), and the fitted regressions are uniformly \(L_4\)-bounded by hypothesis. For each residual term, clipping, the Lipschitz bound for \((u,v)\mapsto u/v\) on \([\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]^2\), and H"older's inequality yield \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\left(\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}-\frac{p_{g,1}}{p_{a,s}}\right)(\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\left(\|\widetilde p_{g,1}-p_{g,1}\|_{P_X,4}+\|\widetilde p_{a,s}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\right)\|\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O_P(a_n),\] and \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}(\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\|\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(b_n).\] The fitted target-contrast term is bounded by the sum of its four regression errors. Conditional score bias is bounded by \(C_\varepsilon\max_{p,m}\|\widehat p-p\|_{P_X,2}\|\widehat m-m\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(a_nb_n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\); foldwise independence makes every centered validation-fold plug-in fluctuation \(o_P(1)\) after \(n^{-1/2}\) summation. The empirical target share is root-\(n\) consistent, lies in the interior clipping region with probability tending to one, and its ratio expansion supplies exactly the target-share term in \(\Psi\). Therefore, uniformly over the fixed score coordinates, \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\mu-B\Theta(P)\}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1),\qquad \max_{1\le j\le M}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\}^2=o_P(1).\]

defs.def:joint-estimator:
For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and observation \(i\), first set \(\widetilde p_{a,s,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde p_{g,1,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{g,1,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde\pi_{g,1}=C_\varepsilon(n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_j=g,S_j=1\})\), and \(\widehat d_{k,c,i}=\widehat m_{g,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{g,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{c,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)+\widehat m_{c,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\). Define \[\widehat A_{i,k,c}=\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\widehat d_{k,c,i}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\},\qquad \widehat\mu_{k,c}=\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat A_{i,k,c}}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}},\] and display the fitted influence coordinate \[\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}=\frac{1}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\{\widehat d_{k,c,i}-\widehat\mu_{k,c}\}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\}\right].\] Stack \(\widehat\mu_{k,c}\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}\). Set \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_i\widehat\Psi_i^{\prime}\), \(\widehat\Omega=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^M}(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}})\), and \(\widehat\Omega_\lambda=\widehat\Omega+n^{-1/4}I_M\). For each \(k\), set \(\widehat b_k^{\mathrm{sep}}=\omega_k\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\), and set \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega\). Finally, \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\). Define the feasible constant-score-span efficiency-loss diagnostic by
\[
\widehat\Delta=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
\widehat\Omega
(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}).
\]
Every denominator and inverse in this construction is defined for every realized sample, and \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) because \(\widehat\Omega\) is positive semidefinite.
defs.def:separate-loading: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \[(b^{\mathrm{sep}})_k=\omega_k\frac{\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1},\] and \(b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) stacks these blocks. This is exactly the loading produced by optimizing each group-event cell separately and then applying \(\omega\).

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), impose the theorem-level foldwise independence, fitted-regression \(L_4\) envelope, propensity and regression \(L_4\) rates, and product-rate condition. The score expansion lemma gives \(D_{i,j}=\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\) with \(\max_j n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2=o_P(1)\). For every \(1\le j,q\le M\), expand the exact displayed covariance estimator entrywise as \[\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}=\left\{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right\}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,j}\widehat\Psi_{i,q}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)D_{i,q}.\] The oracle empirical-covariance fluctuation is \(o_P(1)\) by i.i.d. sampling and the fourth-moment envelopes. Cauchy--Schwarz gives \[\begin{aligned}|\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}|&\le\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right|\\&\quad+\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}+\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\Psi_j(O_i)^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}=o_P(1),\end{aligned}\] where \(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_{i,q}^2=O_P(1)\) follows from \(\widehat\Psi_{i,q}=\Psi_q(O_i)+D_{i,q}\). Since \(M\) is fixed, \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M\max_{j,q}|A_{jq}|\) passes entrywise convergence to operator norm. Because \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^M\) and positive-semidefinite projection is nonexpansive in Frobenius norm, \[\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),\qquad \|\widehat\Omega_\lambda-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\lambda_n=o_P(1).\]

The aggregate formed from the Ortiz-Villavicencio--Sant'Anna componentwise-GMM ATT functionals using the prespecified weights is joint-optimal in the constant retained-score span if and only if \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), equivalently if and only if each block of \(\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) is constant across the comparison cohorts in that block. \[
V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}
=(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}(N^{\prime}\Omega N)^{-1}(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})
=(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})
\]
holds without learner conditions. Suppose in addition that the i.i.d. sampling, fixed-fold sample splitting, fitted-regression \(L_4(P_X)\) envelope, propensity and regression \(L_4(P_X)\) rates, product-rate condition, and deterministic ridge condition of Theorem \(\ref{thm:joint-system-limit}\) all hold. For \(g=2\), all covariance entries use the defined baseline period \(1\). If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), then \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}=b^{\mathrm{sep}}\), and \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\), reproducing within-cell GMM optimality.

snapshot.stmt: The primitive law class is nonempty for a feasible common overlap constant. Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3\}\), \(\omega_{(2,2)}=1\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/2\). Let \(X_i=x_0\) almost surely; let \((G_i,S_i)\) be uniform on \(\{(2,0),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1)\}\); and independently let \(U_{i1},U_{i2},U_{i3}\) be independent Rademacher variables. Set \(Y_{it}(a,s)=U_{it}/8\) for every \(a\in\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), and \(t\in\{1,2,3\}\), and set \(Y_{it}=Y_{it}(G_i,S_i)\). The induced full-data law \(Q_0\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\): all four retained disjoint cells have probability \(1/4>\varepsilon\), the causal restrictions hold with zero effects and common trends, \(m_{a,s,(2,2)}=0\), and the sole centered score equals \(4\sigma_{a,s}^{2,3}\{U_{i2}-U_{i1}\}/8\) on cell \((a,s)\). Consequently, \(\Omega=1/2\), so \(\kappa I_1\preceq\Omega\preceq\kappa^{-1}I_1\), while the outcome and true-regression fourth-moment bounds hold.

defs.def:ddd-law-class: \(\mathcal M=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathsf W): Q\text{ satisfies consistency, no anticipation, no ineligible spillover, every retained pairwise conditional DDD restriction, cell overlap with }0<\varepsilon<1/4,\text{ and, for }P=Q_O,\text{ the outcome fourth-moment and score-spectrum bounds}\}\). The class contains only primitive restrictions on \(Q\) and its observed-data pushforward \(P\); conditional Jensen's inequality and overlap imply the needed true-regression moments. Independent sampling, cross-fitting, learner rates, and fitted-regression tightness are theorem-level conditions or consequences, not members of the law class.
defs.def:pairwise-score: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), set \[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)=\Theta_k(P)+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\pi_{g,1}}\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}+\frac{p_{g,1}(X_i)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{p_{a,s}(X_i)}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\}.\] Thus \(R_{k,c}-\Theta_k(P)\) is the observed-data first-order influence of the Hájek-ratio pairwise estimator, including estimation of \(\pi_{g,1}\).
defs.def:observable-functional: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), define \[\Theta_k(P)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal J_k|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal J_k}\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}},\qquad \Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)=\omega^{\prime}\Theta(P).\] Both quantities are functionals only of the observed-data law \(P=Q_O\).

assumptions.ass:no-anticipation: \(Q\{Y_{it}(g,1)=Y_{it}(\infty,1)\text{ for every }g\in\mathcal G\text{ and }t\in\mathcal T\text{ with }t<g\}=1\).
assumptions.ass:pairwise-conditional-ddd: For every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\) with \(2\le g\le t\le T\), every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(Q_X\)-almost every \(x\), \(E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,1)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,1)\mid G_i=g,S_i=1,X_i=x]-E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,0)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,0)\mid G_i=g,S_i=0,X_i=x]=E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,1)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,1)\mid G_i=c,S_i=1,X_i=x]-E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,0)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,0)\mid G_i=c,S_i=0,X_i=x]\).
assumptions.ass:cell-overlap: For every cohort-eligibility cell \((a,s)\) entering a retained comparison, \(Q(G_i=a,S_i=s\mid X_i=x)\ge\varepsilon\) for \(Q_X\)-almost every \(x\).

snapshot.stmt: For every full-data law \(Q\in\mathcal M\), let \(P=Q_O=Q\circ o^{-1}\). For every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), \[\theta_k(Q)=\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}}=E_P[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)].\] Consequently, \(\theta(Q)=\Theta(P)\), \(\tau_\omega(Q)=\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\), \(E_P[R(O_i;\eta_0)]=B\Theta(P)\), and \(E_P[\Psi(O_i)]=0\). For the earliest admissible cohort \(g=2\), every displayed change uses the defined baseline \(g-1=1\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with observed-data law \(P=Q_O\), \(\Omega=\Omega^{\mathrm{DDD}}\). defs.def:shared-covariance: For score coordinates \(j=(k,c)\) and \(q=(\ell,d)\), let \(g_k\) and \(g_\ell\) denote the first components of \(k\) and \(\ell\), and define \[\Omega^{\mathrm{DDD}}_{j q}=E_P\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{g_k=g_\ell\}p_{g_k,1}(X_i)\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}\{d_{\ell,d}(X_i)-\Theta_\ell(P)\}}{\pi_{g_k,1}\pi_{g_\ell,1}}+\sum_{a,s}p_{a,s}(X_i)L_{k,c}^{a,s}(X_i)L_{\ell,d}^{a,s}(X_i)v_{a,s;k\ell}(X_i)\right].\] The sum ranges over cohort-eligibility cells entering both score coordinates.

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), suppose the off-fold learners satisfy foldwise independence, the fitted-regression \(L_4(P_X)\) envelope, \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\), \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\), \(a_n\to0\), \(b_n\to0\), and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). Four disjoint cells enter each retained pairwise score, so overlap and \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\) give \(p_{a,s}(x)\in[\varepsilon,1-3\varepsilon]\subset[\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]\) for every retained cell. Hence \(C_\varepsilon(p_{a,s})=p_{a,s}\), the clipping map is one-Lipschitz, and \[\|\widetilde p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\le\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n).\] The outcome and true-regression fourth-moment envelopes give \(\|\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O(1)\), and the fitted regressions are uniformly \(L_4\)-bounded by hypothesis. For each residual term, clipping, the Lipschitz bound for \((u,v)\mapsto u/v\) on \([\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]^2\), and H"older's inequality yield \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\left(\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}-\frac{p_{g,1}}{p_{a,s}}\right)(\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\left(\|\widetilde p_{g,1}-p_{g,1}\|_{P_X,4}+\|\widetilde p_{a,s}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\right)\|\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O_P(a_n),\] and \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}(\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\|\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(b_n).\] The fitted target-contrast term is bounded by the sum of its four regression errors. Conditional score bias is bounded by \(C_\varepsilon\max_{p,m}\|\widehat p-p\|_{P_X,2}\|\widehat m-m\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(a_nb_n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\); foldwise independence makes every centered validation-fold plug-in fluctuation \(o_P(1)\) after \(n^{-1/2}\) summation. The empirical target share is root-\(n\) consistent, lies in the interior clipping region with probability tending to one, and its ratio expansion supplies exactly the target-share term in \(\Psi\). Therefore, uniformly over the fixed score coordinates, \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\mu-B\Theta(P)\}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1),\qquad \max_{1\le j\le M}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\}^2=o_P(1).\]

defs.def:joint-estimator:
For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and observation \(i\), first set \(\widetilde p_{a,s,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde p_{g,1,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{g,1,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde\pi_{g,1}=C_\varepsilon(n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_j=g,S_j=1\})\), and \(\widehat d_{k,c,i}=\widehat m_{g,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{g,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{c,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)+\widehat m_{c,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\). Define \[\widehat A_{i,k,c}=\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\widehat d_{k,c,i}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\},\qquad \widehat\mu_{k,c}=\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat A_{i,k,c}}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}},\] and display the fitted influence coordinate \[\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}=\frac{1}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\{\widehat d_{k,c,i}-\widehat\mu_{k,c}\}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\}\right].\] Stack \(\widehat\mu_{k,c}\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}\). Set \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_i\widehat\Psi_i^{\prime}\), \(\widehat\Omega=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^M}(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}})\), and \(\widehat\Omega_\lambda=\widehat\Omega+n^{-1/4}I_M\). For each \(k\), set \(\widehat b_k^{\mathrm{sep}}=\omega_k\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\), and set \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega\). Finally, \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\). Define the feasible constant-score-span efficiency-loss diagnostic by
\[
\widehat\Delta=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
\widehat\Omega
(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}).
\]
Every denominator and inverse in this construction is defined for every realized sample, and \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) because \(\widehat\Omega\) is positive semidefinite.
defs.def:separate-loading: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \[(b^{\mathrm{sep}})_k=\omega_k\frac{\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1},\] and \(b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) stacks these blocks. This is exactly the loading produced by optimizing each group-event cell separately and then applying \(\omega\).

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), impose the theorem-level foldwise independence, propensity and regression \(L_4(P_X)\) rates, and product-rate condition. No separate true- or fitted-regression envelope is imposed: the score-expansion lemma derives the required envelopes from the primitive outcome fourth moment, overlap, and the regression error rate. That lemma gives \(D_{i,j}=\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\) with \(\max_j n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2=o_P(1)\). For every \(1\le j,q\le M\), \[\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}=\left\{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right\}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,j}\widehat\Psi_{i,q}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)D_{i,q}.\] The oracle empirical-covariance fluctuation is \(o_P(1)\) by i.i.d. sampling and the derived fourth-moment bound. Cauchy--Schwarz gives \[\begin{aligned}|\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}|&\le\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right|\\&\quad+\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}+\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\Psi_j(O_i)^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}=o_P(1).\end{aligned}\] Since \(M\) is fixed, \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M\max_{j,q}|A_{jq}|\) passes entrywise convergence to operator norm. Because \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^M\) and positive-semidefinite projection is nonexpansive in Frobenius norm, \[\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),\qquad \|\widehat\Omega_\lambda-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\lambda_n=o_P(1).\]

=(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})

 \mathscr E_+=\{[\mathfrak H(P)]:N^{\prime}\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)\ne0\}.
\]
For invariants induced by compatible laws in \(\mathcal M\), the joint variance gain is zero on \(\mathscr E_0\) and strictly positive on \(\mathscr E_+\). This partition is an evaluable restatement of the separate-joint frontier, not an independent or explanatory classification.

The strict class is nonempty even in the smallest architecture. Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/8\). For any prespecified \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)^{\prime}\) with \(\omega_1+\omega_2=1\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\), there is a bounded compatible full-data law \(Q\in\mathcal M\) for which, in the coordinate order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
 \Omega=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 3/8&3/16&0\\
 3/16&3/8&3/32\\
 0&3/32&3/8
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 b^{\mathrm{sep}}=(\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)^{\prime},
\]

\[

defs.def:ddd-law-class: \(\mathcal M=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathsf W): Q\text{ satisfies consistency, no anticipation, no ineligible spillover, every retained pairwise conditional DDD restriction, cell overlap with }0<\varepsilon<1/4,\text{ and, for }P=Q_O,\text{ the outcome fourth-moment and score-spectrum bounds}\}\). defs.def:labelled-incidence-handle: Expand every score coordinate \(j=((g,t),c)\in\mathcal I\) into the cohort-eligibility-time residual coordinates \(\rho=(a,s,u)\in\mathcal R\), attach the signed functional coefficient \(A_{j\rho}(x)\), and retain \(\mathfrak H(P)=(\mathcal I,(\mathcal J_k)_k,\mathcal R,A,\omega,\mathfrak C(P),N)\). Recover \(\Omega(P)=\mathfrak C(P)\), compute the published componentwise loading blockwise, and evaluate \(N^{\prime}\Omega(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)\). For the smallest strict-gap search, specialize to \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), and \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\); parameterize bounded cell residuals and target-cell contrasts, enforce the causal restrictions, compute the resulting \(3\times3\) positive-definite \(\Omega\), and determine the variance-gap quadratic form exactly.
defs.def:pairwise-score: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), set \[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)=\Theta_k(P)+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\pi_{g,1}}\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}+\frac{p_{g,1}(X_i)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{p_{a,s}(X_i)}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\}.\] Thus \(R_{k,c}-\Theta_k(P)\) is the observed-data first-order influence of the Hájek-ratio pairwise estimator, including estimation of \(\pi_{g,1}\).
defs.def:observable-functional: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), define \[\Theta_k(P)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal J_k|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal J_k}\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}},\qquad \Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)=\omega^{\prime}\Theta(P).\] Both quantities are functionals only of the observed-data law \(P=Q_O\).
defs.def:shared-covariance: For score coordinates \(j=(k,c)\) and \(q=(\ell,d)\), let \(g_k\) and \(g_\ell\) denote the first components of \(k\) and \(\ell\), and define \[\Omega^{\mathrm{DDD}}_{j q}=E_P\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{g_k=g_\ell\}p_{g_k,1}(X_i)\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}\{d_{\ell,d}(X_i)-\Theta_\ell(P)\}}{\pi_{g_k,1}\pi_{g_\ell,1}}+\sum_{a,s}p_{a,s}(X_i)L_{k,c}^{a,s}(X_i)L_{\ell,d}^{a,s}(X_i)v_{a,s;k\ell}(X_i)\right].\] The sum ranges over cohort-eligibility cells entering both score coordinates.
defs.def:separate-loading: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \[(b^{\mathrm{sep}})_k=\omega_k\frac{\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1},\] and \(b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) stacks these blocks. Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/8\). Fix \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)^{\prime}\) with \(\omega_1+\omega_2=1\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\). For every

0<|\rho|<\frac{\sqrt7}{3}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad

\end{pmatrix},
\qquad

\omega_2
\end{pmatrix},

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\), let \(P=Q_O\). Suppose the off-fold learners satisfy foldwise independence, \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\), \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\), \(a_n\to0\), \(b_n\to0\), and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). These learner sequences and rates are supplied as theorem-level conditional hypotheses; no uniform learner-achievability claim over \(\mathcal M\) is made. No fitted-regression envelope is separately assumed, because it follows from the primitive outcome fourth moment, overlap, and the regression error rate. Use the deterministic ridge \(\lambda_n=n^{-1/4}>0\). The score expansion and covariance lemmas then derive, rather than assume, \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}-\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\}=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n(b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1)\rightsquigarrow N(0,V_{\mathrm{joint}}),\qquad \|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1).\] Moreover, \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}\) is the unique minimizer of \(b^{\prime}\Omega b\) over constant \(b\in\mathbb R^M\) satisfying \(B^{\prime}b=\omega\), \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\to_Pb^{\mathrm{joint}}\), \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{joint}}>0\), and \[\lim_{n\to\infty}P\{\tau_\omega(Q)\in\mathcal C_{n,1-\alpha}\}=1-\alpha.\] These are efficiency and inference claims only within the finite constant span of the retained pairwise scores, not a semiparametric efficiency bound for the full conditional-moment model. If a target coordinate has \(g=2\), its score and fitted score use \(\Delta Y_{i,k}=Y_{it}-Y_{i1}\). If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), the joint loading, estimator, and variance reduce to the published within-\(k\) comparison-cohort GMM objects. The zero-variance convention in Definition \(\ref{def:wald-interval}\) totalizes the finite-sample interval and is asymptotically inactive.

defs.def:joint-estimator:
For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and observation \(i\), first set \(\widetilde p_{a,s,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde p_{g,1,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{g,1,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde\pi_{g,1}=C_\varepsilon(n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_j=g,S_j=1\})\), and \(\widehat d_{k,c,i}=\widehat m_{g,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{g,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{c,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)+\widehat m_{c,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\). Define \[\widehat A_{i,k,c}=\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\widehat d_{k,c,i}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\},\qquad \widehat\mu_{k,c}=\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat A_{i,k,c}}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}},\] and display the fitted influence coordinate \[\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}=\frac{1}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\{\widehat d_{k,c,i}-\widehat\mu_{k,c}\}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\}\right].\] Stack \(\widehat\mu_{k,c}\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}\). Set \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_i\widehat\Psi_i^{\prime}\), \(\widehat\Omega=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^M}(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}})\), and \(\widehat\Omega_\lambda=\widehat\Omega+n^{-1/4}I_M\). For each \(k\), set \(\widehat b_k^{\mathrm{sep}}=\omega_k\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\), and set \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega\). Finally, \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\). Define the feasible constant-score-span efficiency-loss diagnostic by
\[
\widehat\Delta=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
\widehat\Omega
(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}).
\]
Every denominator and inverse in this construction is defined for every realized sample, and \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) because \(\widehat\Omega\) is positive semidefinite.

defs.def:wald-interval: Let \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) be the \(1-\alpha/2\) quantile of \(N(0,1)\) and define \[\mathcal C_{n,1-\alpha}=\left[\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}-z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}/n},\;\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}+z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}/n}\right].\] If \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\), define the estimated standard error to be zero, do not divide by it, and set \(\mathcal C_{n,1-\alpha}=\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}\}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\), and \(M\). The aggregate formed from the Ortiz-Villavicencio--Sant'Anna componentwise-GMM ATT functionals using the prespecified weights is joint-optimal in the constant retained-score span if and only if \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), equivalently if and only if each block of \(\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) is constant across the comparison cohorts in that block. For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\), with \(P=Q_O\), the population identity
\[
V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}
=(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}(N^{\prime}\Omega N)^{-1}(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})
=(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})
\]
holds without learner conditions, with the zero-dimensional quadratic interpreted as zero. Suppose in addition that the i.i.d. sampling, fixed-fold sample splitting, propensity and regression \(L_4(P_X)\) rates, product-rate condition, and deterministic ridge condition of Theorem \(\ref{thm:joint-system-limit}\) all hold. The learner sequences and rates are theorem-level conditional hypotheses, and no uniform learner-achievability claim over \(\mathcal M\) is made; no separate fitted-regression envelope is required. Then \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}\) and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}\) have asymptotic variances \(V_{\mathrm{joint}}\) and \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}\), respectively, so the joint estimator has strictly smaller asymptotic variance exactly when the net cross-block covariance contribution is nonconstant across comparison cohorts within at least one group-event block. Moreover, \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) for every realized sample and \(\widehat\Delta\to_P V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}\). Thus \(\widehat\Delta\) is a consistent descriptive diagnostic of the constant retained-score-span efficiency loss; no convergence rate, test, confidence interval, or full semiparametric-efficiency claim is made. For \(g=2\), all covariance entries use the defined baseline period \(1\). If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), then \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}=b^{\mathrm{sep}}\), and \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\), reproducing within-cell GMM optimality.

For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and observation \(i\), first set \(\widetilde p_{a,s,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde p_{g,1,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{g,1,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde\pi_{g,1}=C_\varepsilon(n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_j=g,S_j=1\})\), and \(\widehat d_{k,c,i}=\widehat m_{g,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{g,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{c,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)+\widehat m_{c,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\). Define \[\widehat A_{i,k,c}=\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\widehat d_{k,c,i}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\},\qquad \widehat\mu_{k,c}=\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat A_{i,k,c}}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}},\] and display the fitted influence coordinate \[\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}=\frac{1}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\{\widehat d_{k,c,i}-\widehat\mu_{k,c}\}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\}\right].\] Stack \(\widehat\mu_{k,c}\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}\). Set \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_i\widehat\Psi_i^{\prime}\), \(\widehat\Omega=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^M}(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}})\), and \(\widehat\Omega_\lambda=\widehat\Omega+n^{-1/4}I_M\). For each \(k\), set \(\widehat b_k^{\mathrm{sep}}=\omega_k\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\), and set \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega\). Finally, \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\). Define the feasible constant-score-span efficiency-loss diagnostic by
\[
\widehat\Delta=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
\widehat\Omega
(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}).
\]
Every denominator and inverse in this construction is defined for every realized sample, and \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) because \(\widehat\Omega\) is positive semidefinite.
defs.def:separate-loading: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \[(b^{\mathrm{sep}})_k=\omega_k\frac{\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1},\] and \(b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) stacks these blocks. This is exactly the loading produced by optimizing each group-event cell separately and then applying \(\omega\).
defs.def:pairwise-score: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), set \[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)=\Theta_k(P)+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\pi_{g,1}}\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}+\frac{p_{g,1}(X_i)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{p_{a,s}(X_i)}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\}.\] Thus \(R_{k,c}-\Theta_k(P)\) is the observed-data first-order influence of the Hájek-ratio pairwise estimator, including estimation of \(\pi_{g,1}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Because \(\mathfrak H(P)\) retains \(\mathfrak C(P)=\Omega(P)\), \(N\), \(\omega\), the comparison labels, and the covariance data, the map \([\mathfrak H(P)]\mapsto N^{\prime}\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)\) is evaluable and constant on label-preserving equivalence classes. Consequently the classes admit the bookkeeping partition
\[
 \mathscr E_0=\{[\mathfrak H(P)]:N^{\prime}\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)=0\},
 \qquad
 \mathscr E_+=\{[\mathfrak H(P)]:N^{\prime}\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)\ne0\}.
\]
For invariants induced by compatible laws in \(\mathcal M\), the joint variance gain is zero on \(\mathscr E_0\) and strictly positive on \(\mathscr E_+\). This partition is an evaluable restatement of the separate-joint frontier, not an independent or explanatory classification.

The strict class is nonempty even in the smallest architecture. Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/8\). For any prespecified \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)^{\prime}\) with \(\omega_1+\omega_2=1\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\), there is a bounded compatible full-data law \(Q\in\mathcal M\) for which, in the coordinate order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
 \Omega=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 3/8&3/16&0\\
 3/16&3/8&3/32\\
 0&3/32&3/8
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 b^{\mathrm{sep}}=(\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)^{\prime},
\]
and
\[
 V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=\frac{3\omega_2^2}{128}>0.
\]
Indeed this witness is one point of the open nonzero-effect family in Theorem \(\ref{thm:open-strict-gap-family}\).

defs.def:labelled-incidence-handle: Expand every score coordinate \(j=((g,t),c)\in\mathcal I\) into the cohort-eligibility-time residual coordinates \(\rho=(a,s,u)\in\mathcal R\), attach the signed functional coefficient \(A_{j\rho}(x)\), and retain \(\mathfrak H(P)=(\mathcal I,(\mathcal J_k)_k,\mathcal R,A,\omega,\mathfrak C(P),N)\). Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/8\). Fix \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)^{\prime}\) with \(\omega_1+\omega_2=1\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\). For every
\[
0<|\rho|<\frac{\sqrt7}{3}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
0<|\delta|<\frac18,
\]
there is a bounded compatible law \(Q_{\rho,\delta}\in\mathcal M\), with nonzero constant post-adoption effects equal to \(\delta\), for which, in the coordinate order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
\Omega(\rho)=
\begin{pmatrix}
3/8&3/16&0\\
3/16&3/8&3\rho/16\\
0&3\rho/16&3/8
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
b^{\mathrm{sep}}=
\begin{pmatrix}\omega_1/2\\ \omega_1/2\\ \omega_2\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
b^{\mathrm{joint}}=
\begin{pmatrix}
\omega_1/2+\rho\omega_2/2\\
\omega_1/2-\rho\omega_2/2\\
\omega_2
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}
=\frac{3\rho^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0.
\]
Thus the smallest architecture contains a nondegenerate open two-parameter family of strict-gap laws, rather than only a zero-effect isolated witness.

snapshot.stmt: The primitive law class is nonempty for a feasible common overlap constant. Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3\}\), \(\omega_{(2,2)}=1\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/2\). Let \(X_i=x_0\) almost surely; let \((G_i,S_i)\) be uniform on \(\{(2,0),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1)\}\); and independently let \(U_{i1},U_{i2},U_{i3}\) be independent Rademacher variables. Set \(Y_{it}(a,s)=U_{it}/8\) for every \(a\in\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), and \(t\in\{1,2,3\}\), and set \(Y_{it}=Y_{it}(G_i,S_i)\). The induced full-data law \(Q_0\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\): all four retained disjoint cells have probability \(1/4>\varepsilon\), the causal restrictions hold with zero effects and common trends, \(m_{a,s,(2,2)}=0\), and the sole centered score equals \(4\sigma_{a,s}^{2,3}\{U_{i2}-U_{i1}\}/8\) on cell \((a,s)\). Consequently, \(\Omega=1/2\), so \(\kappa I_1\preceq\Omega\preceq\kappa^{-1}I_1\), while the outcome and true-regression fourth-moment bounds hold.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with observed-data law \(P=Q_O\), \(\Omega=\Omega^{\mathrm{DDD}}\). snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), suppose the off-fold learners satisfy foldwise independence, \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\), \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\), \(a_n\to0\), \(b_n\to0\), and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). These learner sequences and rates are theorem-level conditional hypotheses; no uniform learner-achievability claim over \(\mathcal M\) is made. Four disjoint cells enter each retained pairwise score, so overlap and \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\) give \(p_{a,s}(x)\in[\varepsilon,1-3\varepsilon]\subset[\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]\) for every retained cell. Hence \(C_\varepsilon(p_{a,s})=p_{a,s}\), the clipping map is one-Lipschitz, and \[\|\widetilde p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\le\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n).\] The primitive outcome fourth moment and overlap imply by conditional Jensen's inequality that every retained true regression is \(L_4(P_X)\)-bounded and that \(\|\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O(1)\). The triangle inequality and the stated regression error rate then give \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(1)\); no separate true- or fitted-regression envelope is assumed. For each residual term, clipping, the Lipschitz bound for \((u,v)\mapsto u/v\) on \([\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]^2\), and H"older's inequality yield \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\left(\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}-\frac{p_{g,1}}{p_{a,s}}\right)(\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\left(\|\widetilde p_{g,1}-p_{g,1}\|_{P_X,4}+\|\widetilde p_{a,s}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\right)\|\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O_P(a_n),\] and \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}(\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\|\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(b_n).\] The fitted target-contrast term is bounded by the sum of its four regression errors. Conditional score bias is bounded by \(C_\varepsilon\max_{p,m}\|\widehat p-p\|_{P_X,2}\|\widehat m-m\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(a_nb_n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\); foldwise independence makes every centered validation-fold plug-in fluctuation \(o_P(1)\) after \(n^{-1/2}\) summation. The empirical target share is root-\(n\) consistent, lies in the interior clipping region with probability tending to one, and its ratio expansion supplies exactly the target-share term in \(\Psi\). Therefore, uniformly over the fixed score coordinates, \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\mu-B\Theta(P)\}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1),\qquad \max_{1\le j\le M}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\}^2=o_P(1).\]

defs.def:joint-estimator:
For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and observation \(i\), first set \(\widetilde p_{a,s,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde p_{g,1,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{g,1,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde\pi_{g,1}=C_\varepsilon(n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_j=g,S_j=1\})\), and \(\widehat d_{k,c,i}=\widehat m_{g,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{g,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{c,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)+\widehat m_{c,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\). Define \[\widehat A_{i,k,c}=\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\widehat d_{k,c,i}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\},\qquad \widehat\mu_{k,c}=\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat A_{i,k,c}}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}},\] and display the fitted influence coordinate \[\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}=\frac{1}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\{\widehat d_{k,c,i}-\widehat\mu_{k,c}\}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\}\right].\] Stack \(\widehat\mu_{k,c}\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}\). Set \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_i\widehat\Psi_i^{\prime}\), \(\widehat\Omega=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^M}(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}})\), and \(\widehat\Omega_\lambda=\widehat\Omega+n^{-1/4}I_M\). For each \(k\), set \(\widehat b_k^{\mathrm{sep}}=\omega_k\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\), and set \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega\). \[
\widehat\Delta=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
\widehat\Omega
(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}).
\]
Every denominator and inverse in this construction is defined for every realized sample, and \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) because \(\widehat\Omega\) is positive semidefinite.

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), impose the theorem-level foldwise independence, propensity and regression \(L_4(P_X)\) rates, and product-rate condition. No separate true- or fitted-regression envelope is imposed: the score-expansion lemma derives the required envelopes from the primitive outcome fourth moment, overlap, and the regression error rate. That lemma gives \(D_{i,j}=\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\) with \(\max_j n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2=o_P(1)\). For every \(1\le j,q\le M\), \[\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}=\left\{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right\}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,j}\widehat\Psi_{i,q}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)D_{i,q}.\] The oracle empirical-covariance fluctuation is \(o_P(1)\) by i.i.d. sampling and the derived fourth-moment bound. Cauchy--Schwarz gives \[\begin{aligned}|\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}|&\le\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right|\\&\quad+\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}+\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\Psi_j(O_i)^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}=o_P(1).\end{aligned}\] Since \(M\) is fixed, \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M\max_{j,q}|A_{jq}|\) passes entrywise convergence to operator norm. snapshot.stmt:
Because \(\mathfrak H(P)\) retains \(\mathfrak C(P)=\Omega(P)\), \(N\), \(\omega\), the comparison labels, and the covariance data, the map \([\mathfrak H(P)]\mapsto N^{\prime}\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)\) is evaluable and constant on label-preserving equivalence classes. Consequently the classes admit the bookkeeping partition
\[
 \mathscr E_0=\{[\mathfrak H(P)]:N^{\prime}\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)=0\},
 \qquad
 \mathscr E_+=\{[\mathfrak H(P)]:N^{\prime}\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)\ne0\}.
\]
For invariants induced by compatible laws in \(\mathcal M\), the joint variance gain is zero on \(\mathscr E_0\) and strictly positive on \(\mathscr E_+\). This partition is an evaluable restatement of the separate-joint frontier, not an independent or explanatory classification.

The strict class is nonempty even in the smallest architecture. Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/8\). For any prespecified \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)^{\prime}\) with \(\omega_1+\omega_2=1\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\), there is a bounded compatible full-data law \(Q\in\mathcal M\) for which, in the coordinate order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
 \Omega=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 3/8&3/16&0\\
 3/16&3/8&3/32\\
 0&3/32&3/8
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 b^{\mathrm{sep}}=(\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)^{\prime},
\]
and
\[
 V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=\frac{3\omega_2^2}{128}>0.
\]
Indeed this witness is one point of the open nonzero-effect family in Theorem \(\ref{thm:open-strict-gap-family}\).

defs.def:ddd-law-class: \(\mathcal M=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathsf W): Q\text{ satisfies consistency, no anticipation, no ineligible spillover, every retained pairwise conditional DDD restriction, cell overlap with }0<\varepsilon<L_{\mathrm{ret}}^{-1},\text{ and, for }P=Q_O,\text{ the outcome fourth-moment and score-spectrum bounds}\}\). The class contains only primitive restrictions on \(Q\) and its observed-data pushforward \(P\); conditional Jensen's inequality and overlap imply the needed true-regression moments. Independent sampling, cross-fitting, learner rates, and fitted-regression tightness are theorem-level conditions or consequences, not members of the law class.
defs.def:labelled-incidence-handle: Expand every score coordinate \(j=((g,t),c)\in\mathcal I\) into the cohort-eligibility-time residual coordinates \(\rho=(a,s,u)\in\mathcal R\), attach the signed functional coefficient \(A_{j\rho}(x)\), and retain \(\mathfrak H(P)=(\mathcal I,(\mathcal J_k)_k,\mathcal R,A,\omega,\mathfrak C(P),N)\). Recover \(\Omega(P)=\mathfrak C(P)\), compute the published componentwise loading blockwise, and evaluate \(N^{\prime}\Omega(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)\). Classify only label-preserving equivalence classes for which the comparison labels, residual labels, signed incidences, aggregate weights, covariance-map entries, and canonical contrast matrix all agree. For the smallest strict-gap search, specialize to \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), and \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\); parameterize bounded cell residuals and target-cell contrasts, enforce the causal restrictions, compute the resulting \(3\times3\) positive-definite \(\Omega\), and determine the variance-gap quadratic form exactly.
defs.def:pairwise-score: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), set \[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)=\Theta_k(P)+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\pi_{g,1}}\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}+\frac{p_{g,1}(X_i)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{p_{a,s}(X_i)}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\}.\] Thus \(R_{k,c}-\Theta_k(P)\) is the observed-data first-order influence of the Hájek-ratio pairwise estimator, including estimation of \(\pi_{g,1}\).
defs.def:observable-functional: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), define \[\Theta_k(P)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal J_k|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal J_k}\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}},\qquad \Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)=\omega^{\prime}\Theta(P).\] Both quantities are functionals only of the observed-data law \(P=Q_O\).
defs.def:shared-covariance: For score coordinates \(j=(k,c)\) and \(q=(\ell,d)\), let \(g_k\) and \(g_\ell\) denote the first components of \(k\) and \(\ell\), and define \[\Omega^{\mathrm{DDD}}_{j q}=E_P\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{g_k=g_\ell\}p_{g_k,1}(X_i)\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}\{d_{\ell,d}(X_i)-\Theta_\ell(P)\}}{\pi_{g_k,1}\pi_{g_\ell,1}}+\sum_{a,s}p_{a,s}(X_i)L_{k,c}^{a,s}(X_i)L_{\ell,d}^{a,s}(X_i)v_{a,s;k\ell}(X_i)\right].\] The sum ranges over cohort-eligibility cells entering both score coordinates.
defs.def:separate-loading: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \[(b^{\mathrm{sep}})_k=\omega_k\frac{\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1},\] and \(b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) stacks these blocks. This is exactly the loading produced by optimizing each group-event cell separately and then applying \(\omega\).
